title: Heat is thermal energy moving between things at different temperatures
summary: Heat is thermal energy moving between two systems that are not at the same temperature.
body: A NASA educator guide says heat describes the transfer of thermal energy between two systems of different temperatures. That transfer moves through solids, liquids, gases, and space. The guide's vocabulary ties thermal energy to faster movement of molecules in a substance. How much energy a particular mug holds is not on the page. A thermometer reading, as a scale, is a different card.

sources.title: NASA's Our World: Insulators, educator guide EG-2010-06-008-LaRC
sources.author: NASA
sources.note: NASA eClips educator guide, U.S. government work, public domain. Product code dated June 2010. Supports heat as transfer of thermal energy between systems at different temperatures, and thermal energy as increased molecular movement.
